## Design patterns

<a id="AbstractFactory"></a>

### Abstract Factory

`AbstractFactory` · `src/patterns.ts:54`

A family of related realizations chosen together, so that members of two families are never mixed (a database and its dialect, an in-memory terminal and the log a scenario reads). In the graph, one choice chooses the whole family.

Source: Gamma et al., Design Patterns (1994), Abstract Factory

A choice that follows it has several ports chosen together.

No choice follows it yet.

<a id="Adapter"></a>

### Adapter

`Adapter` · `src/patterns.ts:29`

A technology made to answer an interface that the product defines, so that the product depends on its own port and only the adapter on the technology: ports and adapters. In the graph, the adapters are implementations, the only nodes that may touch the platform.

Source: A. Cockburn, Hexagonal architecture (ports and adapters), 2005; Gamma et al., Design Patterns (1994), Adapter · `https://alistair.cockburn.us/hexagonal-architecture/`

A choice that follows it has realizations that touch the platform (implementations).

No choice follows it yet.

- Maintained by: trame
- Serves: [Known designs, named](product.md#KnownDesigns)

<a id="Bridge"></a>

### Bridge

`Bridge` · `src/patterns.ts:42`

An abstraction and its implementation vary independently: what answers a port works through another port, and either side can be chosen without the other changing.

Source: Gamma et al., Design Patterns (1994), Bridge

A choice that follows it has realizations that reach another port.

No choice follows it yet.

- Maintained by: trame
- Serves: [Known designs, named](product.md#KnownDesigns)

<a id="Repository"></a>

### Repository

`Repository` · `src/patterns.ts:66`

The domain's objects as a collection behind an interface: what answers it reaches the storage through another port, and holds neither a driver nor a connection. It touches nothing itself.

Source: M. Fowler, Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (2002), Repository (E. Hieatt, R. Mee) · `https://martinfowler.com/eaaCatalog/repository.html`

A choice that follows it has realizations that are functions; realizations that reach another port.

No choice follows it yet.

- Maintained by: trame
- Serves: [Known designs, named](product.md#KnownDesigns)

<a id="Strategy"></a>

### Strategy

`Strategy` · `src/patterns.ts:16` · status: **held**

Interchangeable behaviours behind one interface: the code that uses the interface does not change when another behaviour is chosen. In the graph, the behaviours are functions that implement a port; they touch nothing.

Source: E. Gamma, R. Helm, R. Johnson, J. Vlissides, Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software (1994), Strategy

A choice that follows it has realizations that are functions.
